dedupe_keys.name: global dataset on heat wave exposure due to the urban heat island effect global uhe 2003 2020

description: This 1 km global dataset estimates, for each year from 2003 to 2020, how many person-days of heat wave exposure urban residents suffered and how much of that was caused by the urban heat island. It uses a gap-filled MODIS land surface temperature series, an adaptive threshold to separate urban from rural areas, and separates the effects of background climate, local landscape and urbanisation. The figshare collection has three items: the Google Earth Engine and Python code, 18 yearly rasters of total heat wave exposure and 18 yearly rasters of exposure caused by the heat island, in person-days per year. Coverage: urban settlements worldwide. Access: free on figshare without an account, as the article states. Licence: CC BY 4.0. Caveats: exposure is based on surface temperature, not air temperature; population weighting follows the gridded population used by the authors. Simulation uses are ranking where heat island mitigation in buildings and public space would cut the most exposure, and exposure inputs for heat health risk models. Related records: the SEDAC global urban heat island 2013 dataset and the global UHI intensity dataset.
